title: Hawthorne
dek: The scribe who turns Pristinia’s arguments into counted votes, recorded decisions and an institutional memory.

facts.Record: Public scenes; later status not established

sources: Main quest-RP archive · message anchors below
NPC Master Registry and Recovery Map · recovery lead, checked against raw scenes
body:
Counting and recording

At the early public assembly, Hawthorne counts votes and writes the results on fresh parchment. His work makes a distinction between what someone proposes and what the settlement adopts. Later assemblies show him counting again when a result needs checking; the record depends on repeated, practical work.

Election and ownership

During the later election gathering, he explains eligibility and asks for evidence of property transfers. Pappy’s claimed ownership cannot simply substitute for paperwork Hawthorne has not received. Collective holdings create a difficulty the existing rules do not clearly answer. Hawthorne brings that question to a show of hands rather than treating his own uncertainty as a final legal ruling. The gathering records candidates and ballot questions, not a complete election result.

A scholar’s unfinished work

Hawthorne describes himself as a nonmagical scribe who came from Eovar and now helps Melian and the Elders. His late mentor Fernir’s work on dwarven settlement matters to him personally. He asks adventurers to return to the Old Earth Hills; his interpretations of recovered evidence remain attributed scholarship, not a complete account of the island’s hidden past.

Recorded scenes

  • Recording the assembly’s vote
  • A scribe from Eovar assisting Pristinia
  • Fernir and the unfinished inquiry
  • Candidates and residency questions
  • Collective ownership and a ballot question
  • Counting again
